subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose restart missed-job catch-up controls in public cron config, and should the supported shape be global max/stagger controls, a skip/freshness policy, or no new public config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the root policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and the choice changes restart semantics for existing scheduled jobs.

options.title: Expose narrow global controls
options.body: Approve documented global cron keys based on the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit default-preserving and zero-limit semantics.

options.title: Design skip policy first
options.body: Prefer a global or per-job skip/freshness policy before implementation so user-facing announcement jobs can opt out without changing catch-up defaults globally.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Decline new public config for now and document current restart catch-up behavior plus operational workarounds.

recommendation.title: Expose narrow global controls
recommendation.body: Approve documented global cron keys based on the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit default-preserving and zero-limit semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public config and scheduler-semantics decision, and history shows steipete as committer/refactorer for the restart catch-up path.
